headline: Purchase of 276 Broadway Street for a senior center approved; release of October 6 Flock camera minutes also approved.
summary: Members approved buying 276 Broadway Street for a senior center and approved releasing Flock camera minutes from October 6. A Draper Laboratory vote was moved to the next agenda after an objection. Several requests for reports and studies were also approved.
decisions: Approved releasing the October 6, 2026 executive session minutes on Flock cameras, with 10 yes votes.
Moved the Draper Laboratory agreements to the next agenda after an objection under council rule 27, so no final vote was taken.
Approved asking the City Manager to brief the council on the future of the summer youth program.
Approved asking for an update on public and sustainability council feedback on the specialized building code.
Approved asking for a fire station repair update to the public safety subcommittee.
Approved asking the city clerk to prepare LHA TIF executive session minutes for release after the solicitor's review.
Approved asking for an update on the replanting plan for Centerville and Woodward.
Approved asking for a report on enforcing approved conditions of the appallorchard project and on its permits.
Approved asking the City Manager to explore a residential tax exemption and the good landlord tax abatement.
Approved asking the finance subcommittee and city finance team to meet as needed to prepare for the FY 28 budget.
Approved asking the council to review unreleased executive session minutes and set a timeline for reviewing minutes.
Referred the Boston Gas request to replace a gas main at 217 to 250 Westford Street to the wire inspector for report and recommendation.
Referred the National Grid request for underground electrical conduit for 225 Middlesex Street to the wire inspector for report and recommendation.
Referred the Zayo request for underground fiber optic conduit at 174 South Street to the wire inspector for report and recommendation.
Approved the reappointments of Maria Sheehy, Richard Cody, and James Gaffney, with 10 yes votes on roll call.
Approved the City Manager's request for one out-of-state trip for the Police Department, with 10 yes votes on roll call.
Approved asking the state to approve a plan change to the Acre urban renewal plan for 276 Broadway Street, with 10 yes votes.
Approved a purchase and sales agreement for 276 Broadway Street, the senior center, with 10 yes votes.
Referred property damage claims to the law department for report and recommendation.
Referred a resident's Flock camera concerns to the city manager for report and recommendation.
Referred the request for a handicap parking sign at 57 Weir Street to the transportation engineer for report and recommendation.
Referred the request for a handicap parking sign at 105 Jewett Street to the transportation engineer for report and recommendation.
discussion: Flock camera minutes: Speakers asked the council to release the October 6 minutes and questioned Flock's data sharing and contract terms. They asked that Flock policy be debated and voted on in open session.
Draper Laboratory vote: An objection under council rule 27 said residents had not had enough community engagement on the project. The chair said the item would go to the next agenda.

Bar and restaurant licenses: Members discussed separate bar and restaurant licenses, how to define suitable food, and how to check that food is still served. The license commission was to continue the discussion on Thursday.
appallorchard project enforcement: Members said stormwater and other approval conditions were not being met while work and occupancy continued. They asked who is responsible for enforcing them.
Residential tax exemption: Members discussed a residential tax exemption and the good landlord tax abatement as ways to shift the tax burden. The motion asks only for an exploration of the options.
